lessons.title: Fractions & Decimals Operations
objectives: Perform four operations on fractions and decimals
Apply BODMAS / PEMDAS order of operations
Convert fractions to recurring and terminating decimals
keyPoints: Always find the lowest common denominator for fraction addition/subtraction
In division, invert the divisor and multiply
Align decimal points strictly for vertical operations

lessons.title: Percentages & Percentage Change
objectives: Calculate percentage increase and decrease
Evaluate percentage error = |error| / actual x 100%
keyPoints: Percentage change is always divided by the original value
Percentage error uses absolute error over true value

lessons.title: Ratio & Proportional Sharing
objectives: Express quantities in simplified ratio form
Divide quantities into multi-part ratios
keyPoints: Sum the parts of the ratio first to find value per single share
Verify the sum of allocated shares equals the original total

lessons.title: Profit, Loss & Percentage Margins
objectives: Determine cost price and selling price given profit percentage
Distinguish margin on selling price from markup on cost price
keyPoints: Profit % = (Profit / Cost Price) * 100
Margin % = (Profit / Selling Price) * 100

lessons.title: Simple & Compound Interest Calculations
objectives: Calculate simple interest and principal
Apply compound interest formula across multiple compounding periods
keyPoints: Simple interest grows linearly with time
Compound interest adds accumulated interest into the principal for subsequent cycles

lessons.title: Linear Equations & Word Problems
objectives: Formulate equations from real-world descriptions
Solve linear equations with brackets and fractions
keyPoints: Define variables clearly at the start of working
Clear fractions by multiplying all terms by the LCM of denominators

lessons.title: Linear Inequalities & Number Line Graphs
objectives: Solve multi-step linear inequalities
Represent closed and open interval solutions on a number line
keyPoints: Reverse the inequality sign whenever multiplying or dividing by a negative number
Filled dot represents <= or >=; open circle represents < or >

lessons.title: Simultaneous Equations & Direct/Inverse Variation
objectives: Solve 2-variable linear systems algebraically
Determine constant of proportionality k and form variation equations
keyPoints: Elimination is faster when variable coefficients match or have opposite signs
Direct variation: y = kx; Inverse variation: y = k/x

lessons.title: Quadratic Equations by Factorization
objectives: Identify two factors multiplying to ac and summing to b
Solve quadratic equations using the null factor law
keyPoints: Ensure the equation equals 0 before applying factorization
Product ac and sum b determine the split of the middle term

lessons.title: The Quadratic Formula & Completing the Square
objectives: Complete the square for monic and non-monic quadratics
Substitute into the quadratic formula accurately
keyPoints: Discriminant b^2 - 4ac dictates real, equal, or no real roots
When b is negative, -b becomes positive

lessons.title: Simultaneous Linear & Quadratic Systems
objectives: Isolate a linear variable and substitute into the quadratic expression
Pair corresponding x and y values accurately
keyPoints: Linear-quadratic systems typically produce two coordinate pairs (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)
Substitute back into the linear equation to avoid ambiguous signs

lessons.title: Angles on Lines, Triangles & Polygons
objectives: Calculate interior and exterior angles of regular polygons
Apply parallel line angle rules (alternate, corresponding, interior)
keyPoints: Sum of exterior angles of any convex polygon is always 360 degrees
Each exterior angle of a regular n-gon is 360 / n

lessons.title: Circle Theorems: Subtended Angles & Cyclic Quads
objectives: Apply angle at centre = 2 x angle at circumference
Use angles in same segment are equal
Prove and apply cyclic quadrilateral theorems
keyPoints: Angle in a semicircle is always a right angle (90 degrees)
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary (sum to 180 degrees)

lessons.title: Right-Angled Trigonometry (SOHCAHTOA)
objectives: Identify opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse relative to target angle
Calculate unknown side lengths and angles using trigonometric ratios
keyPoints: $\sin\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}$, $\cos\theta = \frac{\text{Adjacent}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}$, $\tan\theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Adjacent}}$
Use inverse trig functions ($\sin^{-1}$, $\cos^{-1}$, $\tan^{-1}$) when solving for angles

lessons.title: Sine & Cosine Rules for Scalene Triangles
objectives: Apply Sine rule when given a matching side-angle pair
Apply Cosine rule for SAS or SSS triangle problems
keyPoints: Cosine rule: isolate $\cos A = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc}$ when given three sides
Area of triangle = $\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$

lessons.title: Three-Figure Bearings & Angles of Elevation/Depression
objectives: Draw clear bearing diagrams with North arrows at every station
Calculate reverse bearings (back-bearings) by adding or subtracting 180 degrees
keyPoints: Bearings are measured clockwise from North and written with 3 digits (e.g., 045 deg)
Angle of elevation equals angle of depression between two observer stations

lessons.title: Grouped Frequency Distributions: Mean & Modal Class
objectives: Construct grouped frequency distribution tables
Calculate mean using assumed mean or direct formula
keyPoints: Class mark x is the average of lower and upper class limits
Modal class has the highest single frequency count

lessons.title: Cumulative Frequency Curves & Percentiles
objectives: Plot smooth cumulative frequency curves (ogives)
Estimate median, lower quartile Q1, upper quartile Q3, and interquartile range
keyPoints: Always plot cumulative frequency at the UPPER class boundaries, not class midpoints
Interquartile range IQR = Q3 - Q1

lessons.title: Probability Rules & Tree Diagrams
objectives: Calculate theoretical probabilities 0 <= P(E) <= 1
Draw and evaluate probability tree diagrams with and without replacement
keyPoints: Multiply probabilities along tree branches (AND rule)
Add probabilities across separate branches (OR rule)

modules.title: Module 1: CBT Time Management & Quick-Elimination Rules

lessons.title: CBT Time Management & Frequency Distribution
objectives: Allocate time per question band (Round 1 fast solve, Round 2 calculation)
Identify high-frequency calculus and algebra clusters in past exams
keyPoints: Never spend more than 90 seconds on a single question on the first pass
Mark flagged questions and return after clearing straightforward algebra items

lessons.title: Option Elimination via Parity & Back-Substitution
objectives: Eliminate at least two incorrect options before computing full algebra
Use unit digit and sign parity checks on polynomial expansion answers
keyPoints: Plugging in simple test values (x = 0 or 1) eliminates 2 out of 4 options in seconds
Examine constant terms to instantly weed out wrong signs

lessons.title: Surd Rationalization & Conjugate Multiplication
objectives: Rationalize binomial surd denominators without hesitation
Simplify compound surds and extract perfect square factors
keyPoints: Conjugate of a + sqrt(b) is a - sqrt(b)
Multiply numerator and denominator simultaneously to preserve equality

lessons.title: Logarithmic Identities & Base Transformations
objectives: Convert non-standard base logarithms to common or natural bases
Solve logarithmic equations with multiple unknown base subscripts
keyPoints: log(xy) = log x + log y; log(x/y) = log x - log y; log(x^n) = n log x
Arguments of logarithms must always be strictly greater than zero

lessons.title: 2x2 Matrix Determinants & Inverse Matrices
objectives: Calculate 2x2 and 3x3 matrix determinants
Determine values of k for which a matrix is singular (det = 0)
keyPoints: A matrix has no inverse if and only if its determinant is 0 (singular matrix)
Inverse of [[a, b], [c, d]] is 1/(ad - bc) * [[d, -b], [-c, a]]

lessons.title: Cramer's Rule for Solving UTME Linear Systems
objectives: Apply Cramer's determinant rule to solve simultaneous equations
Recognize when systems have unique, infinite, or no solutions
keyPoints: Dx is obtained by replacing column 1 of coefficient matrix with constant column
If D = 0 and Dx != 0, the system has no solutions

lessons.title: Rapid Derivative Rules: Power, Product & Chain
objectives: Differentiate polynomials, rational powers, and trigonometric expressions
Compute rate of change and acceleration problems from displacement functions
keyPoints: Power rule: multiply by exponent and reduce exponent by 1
Velocity v = ds/dt; Acceleration a = dv/dt = d^2s/dt^2

lessons.title: Tangents, Normals & Turning Points
objectives: Find gradient of tangent at specified point x = x0
Determine nature of stationary points using second derivative d^2y/dx^2
keyPoints: Normal gradient m_normal = -1 / m_tangent
d^2y/dx^2 > 0 indicates a local minimum; < 0 indicates a local maximum

lessons.title: Definite Integrals & Area Under Curves
objectives: Integrate polynomial terms: integral x^n dx = x^(n+1)/(n+1) + C
Evaluate definite integrals between boundaries a and b without constant C
keyPoints: Definite integral between limits a and b is F(b) - F(a)
Area below the x-axis produces a negative integral value; take absolute value for geometric area

lessons.title: Parallel & Perpendicular Line Conditions
objectives: Convert general line equations Ax + By + C = 0 into slope-intercept form y = mx + c
Find equation of perpendicular bisector between two coordinates
keyPoints: Slope m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)
Negative reciprocal slope for perpendicularity: m2 = -1 / m1

lessons.title: Permutations (nPr) vs Combinations (nCr)
objectives: Calculate nPr = n! / (n - r)! and nCr = n! / (r!(n - r)!)
Solve word problems involving word anagrams with repeated letters
keyPoints: If arrangement order matters (ranks, words, positions), use Permutation
If grouping order does not matter (committees, handshakes, card hands), use Combination

title: JSS 3 Basic Mathematics & BECE Exam Prep

lessons.title: Directed Numbers & Adding/Subtracting Integers
objectives: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide positive and negative numbers
Avoid double-negative errors in basic arithmetic
keyPoints: Subtracting a negative number is equivalent to adding a positive: -(-b) = +b
Multiplying two negative numbers produces a positive result

lessons.title: Fractions, Decimals & Significant Figures
objectives: Simplify fractions to lowest terms
Round numbers to 1, 2, or 3 significant figures
keyPoints: Leading zeros are never significant (e.g. 0.0042 has 2 significant figures)
Zeros between non-zero digits are always significant

lessons.title: Simple Interest, Discounts & Everyday Money
objectives: Calculate simple interest earned or paid on loans
Determine cash discount and hire purchase total payments
keyPoints: Time T must always be expressed in years
Total amount A = Principal P + Interest I

lessons.title: Expanding Brackets & Collecting Like Terms
objectives: Expand single brackets using distributive property
Expand double brackets using FOIL / grid methods
keyPoints: Sign rule: -a(b - c) = -ab + ac (carefully observe the negative bracket expansion)
Only like terms with identical variable powers can be added together

lessons.title: Simple Linear Equations with Fractions
objectives: Cross-multiply fractional equations accurately
Group variable terms on the left and constant numbers on the right
keyPoints: Multiply both sides by common denominator to eliminate all fractions immediately
Check your answer by substituting back into original equation

lessons.title: Algebraic Factorization by Grouping
objectives: Extract highest common factor (HCF) from algebraic expressions
Factorize expressions like ax + ay + bx + by = (a + b)(x + y)
keyPoints: Group into two pairs that share common factors
Verify the bracket contents are identical after first round of factoring

lessons.title: Angles on Lines, Vertically Opposite & Triangles
objectives: Find missing angles on straight lines and intersections
Apply exterior angle of a triangle equals sum of two opposite interior angles
keyPoints: Vertically opposite angles are equal
Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal

lessons.title: Pythagoras' Theorem in Right Triangles
objectives: State Pythagoras' theorem for right-angled triangles
Compute unknown side lengths to 1 or 2 decimal places
keyPoints: Hypotenuse is always the longest side, opposite the 90 degree right angle
To find a shorter side: a^2 = c^2 - b^2

lessons.title: Perimeter & Area of Parallelograms and Trapezia
objectives: Calculate area of parallelograms using perpendicular height
Calculate area of trapezia given two parallel sides a and b
keyPoints: Height must be strictly perpendicular to the base, not the slanted side length
Express units in cm^2 or m^2 consistently

lessons.title: Volume and Surface Area of Cylinders
objectives: Calculate cylinder volume using radius and height
Evaluate curved surface area 2 * pi * r * h for open and closed cans
keyPoints: Check whether the problem specifies a closed cylinder (2 circular ends) or open (1 end)
Use pi = 22/7 or 3.142 as instructed by question

lessons.title: Mean, Median & Mode of Ungrouped Data
objectives: Calculate arithmetic mean = sum(x) / N
Find median by sorting data in ascending order first
keyPoints: Mode is the value appearing with the highest frequency
If N is even, median is the average of the two middle values

lessons.title: Constructing and Interpreting Pie Charts & Bar Charts
objectives: Calculate sector angles for pie chart construction
Read frequencies from bar charts and histogram bars
keyPoints: Sum of all sector angles in a pie chart must equal 360 degrees exactly
Leave equal gaps between bars in a bar chart to distinguish from continuous histograms

title: Senior Secondary Algebra & Trigonometry Deep Dive

lessons.title: Arithmetic Progressions (AP): nth Term & Sum
objectives: Formulate equations for first term a and common difference d
Calculate sum of arithmetic series across real-world finance contexts
keyPoints: Common difference d = T2 - T1 = T3 - T2
When last term l is known: Sn = n/2(a + l)

lessons.title: Geometric Progressions (GP): nth Term & Sum
objectives: Determine common ratio r = T2 / T1
Apply GP models to population growth and compound financial assets
keyPoints: When |r| < 1, use Sn = a(1 - r^n) / (1 - r)
When |r| > 1, use Sn = a(r^n - 1) / (r - 1)

lessons.title: Sum to Infinity of Convergent Geometric Series
objectives: State the necessary condition for a GP to converge
Express recurring decimals as rational fractions using sum to infinity
keyPoints: A geometric series only has a sum to infinity if -1 < r < 1
If r >= 1 or r <= -1, the series diverges and has no finite sum to infinity

modules.title: Module 2: Quadratic Equations & Nature of Roots

lessons.title: Completing the Square and Expressing in Vertex Form
objectives: Complete the square when coefficient of x^2 is greater than 1
Determine coordinates of vertex and state line of symmetry x = h
keyPoints: Divide by a first when factoring non-monic quadratics
Vertex gives minimum point if a > 0; maximum point if a < 0

lessons.title: Discriminant Analysis & Nature of Roots
objectives: Calculate discriminant value without solving equation completely
Find range of values of constant k for which equation has real roots
keyPoints: For real roots: b^2 - 4ac >= 0
For equal / repeated roots (tangent to x-axis): b^2 - 4ac = 0

lessons.title: Trigonometric Ratios in All Four Quadrants (CAST Rule)
objectives: Identify reference acute angle $\alpha$ for any given angle $\theta$
Apply the CAST diagram (Quadrant 1: All, Quadrant 2: Sin, Quadrant 3: Tan, Quadrant 4: Cos)
keyPoints: Quadrant 2: $\theta = 180^\circ - \alpha$; Quadrant 3: $\theta = 180^\circ + \alpha$; Quadrant 4: $\theta = 360^\circ - \alpha$
$\cos(180^\circ - \theta) = -\cos\theta$; $\sin(180^\circ - \theta) = \sin\theta$

lessons.title: Graphing y = a sin(bx) and y = a cos(bx)
objectives: Plot trigonometric waves from 0 to 360 degrees
State amplitude and period of transformed trigonometric functions
keyPoints: Amplitude is half the vertical distance between maximum and minimum values
Period of sin(bx) or cos(bx) is 360 / b degrees

lessons.title: Advanced Sine and Cosine Rules for Scalene Triangles
objectives: Select correct trigonometric rule based on given side/angle configuration
Resolve ambiguous case of Sine rule when given SSA
keyPoints: Use Cosine rule when two sides and the included angle (SAS) are known
Remember cos(obtuse angle) is negative: a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc(-cos(180 - A))

lessons.title: Three-Figure Bearings & Practical Surveying
objectives: Draw multi-station bearing diagrams with accurate North reference lines
Combine bearings with Cosine rule to calculate direct straight-line distance back to start
keyPoints: Always draw a cross with a North arrow at EVERY landmark mentioned in the question
Internal angles can be calculated using alternate interior angles between parallel North lines

modules.title: Module 1: Numbers, Place Value & Large Operations

lessons.title: Place Value up to Millions & Roman Numerals to M
objectives: Identify place values (Units, Tens, Hundreds, Thousands, Millions)
Convert numbers between Arabic numerals and Roman numerals
keyPoints: Roman numerals: I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100, D = 500, M = 1000
A smaller numeral before a larger one means subtraction: IV = 4, IX = 9, XC = 90

lessons.title: Multiplication & Long Division Word Problems
objectives: Multiply 3-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers
Perform long division step by step (Divide, Multiply, Subtract, Bring down)
keyPoints: Remember DMSB: Divide, Multiply, Subtract, Bring down
Double-check remainders are smaller than the divisor

lessons.title: Fractions: Proper, Improper & Mixed Operations
objectives: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions and vice versa
Apply common denominators to add and subtract fractions
keyPoints: To convert 2 3/4 to improper: (2 * 4 + 3) / 4 = 11/4
In division: Keep the first fraction, Change division to multiplication, Flip the second fraction (KCF)

lessons.title: Percentages of Quantities & Ratio Sharing
objectives: Calculate percentage of items (e.g. 15% of ₦2,000)
Share quantities in ratios like 2 : 3 : 5
keyPoints: Total parts = sum of ratio terms

lessons.title: Cost Price, Selling Price, Profit & Loss
objectives: Calculate profit and loss in Naira and Kobo
Determine selling price given profit percentage
keyPoints: Selling Price = Cost Price + Profit
Selling Price = Cost Price - Loss

lessons.title: Perimeter & Area of Squares and Rectangles
objectives: Calculate perimeter as distance around the boundary
Compute area of rectangles and composite L-shaped figures
keyPoints: Perimeter is measured in linear units (cm, m); Area is measured in square units (cm^2, m^2)
Split composite L-shapes into two distinct rectangles to calculate area

lessons.title: Volume and Capacity of Cubes & Rectangular Boxes
objectives: Calculate volume of cubes (s^3) and cuboids (L * B * H)
Convert 1,000 cm^3 to 1 litre of liquid capacity
keyPoints: Volume is measured in cubic units (cm^3 or m^3)
1 litre = 1,000 cm^3 = 1,000 millilitres (ml)

lessons.title: Finding the Next Term in Number Pattern Sequences
objectives: Identify constant differences between sequence terms
Spot geometric doubling and alternating rule progressions
keyPoints: Look at differences between consecutive terms: +2, +4, +6, +8...
Check if numbers are squares (1, 4, 9, 16, 25) or cubes

lessons.title: Solving Box, Circle & Triangle Quantitative Puzzles
objectives: Test sample diagrams with four basic operations (+, -, *, /)
Apply discovered operational rules to solve missing numbers
keyPoints: Always test your hypothesis on BOTH provided sample diagrams before solving the question
Common sample rules include: (Top * Bottom) / Left = Centre, or (A + B) * (C - D)

title: Cambridge IGCSE Extended Mathematics Complete Guide

lessons.title: Indices, Fractional Powers & Standard Form
objectives: Simplify expressions involving fractional and negative powers
Express numbers in standard form where 1 <= A < 10
keyPoints: Standard form coefficient A must be strictly between 1 and 10

lessons.title: Upper and Lower Bounds & Error Intervals
objectives: Determine upper and lower limits of rounded values
Calculate maximum and minimum possible values of expressions like a / b
keyPoints: To maximize a quotient a / b: use Maximum(a) / Minimum(b)
To minimize a quotient a / b: use Minimum(a) / Maximum(b)

lessons.title: Function Notation: Evaluating f(x) and g(x)
objectives: Evaluate function outputs for numerical and algebraic inputs
Solve equations in function notation f(x) = 0
keyPoints: f(3) means replace every x in the formula with 3
f(x) = 3 means set the entire expression equal to 3 and solve for x

lessons.title: Composite Functions fg(x) and Inverse Functions f^-1(x)
objectives: Form composite functions fg(x) and gf(x)
Find inverse function by setting y = f(x), swapping variables and making y the subject
keyPoints: In fg(x), the inner function g(x) is evaluated first and substituted into f
The graph of an inverse function f^-1(x) is the reflection of f(x) in the line y = x

modules.title: Module 3: Coordinate Geometry & Tangents to Curves

lessons.title: Drawing Tangents to Estimate Gradients of Curves
objectives: Draw accurate tangents at specified point x = x0
Calculate gradient = rise / run from the drawn tangent line
keyPoints: The tangent line touches the curve at exactly one point without crossing through it
Select two points far apart on the tangent line to minimize gradient measurement error

lessons.title: 3D Trigonometry: Angles Between Lines & Planes
objectives: Calculate lengths of space diagonals across cuboids using 3D Pythagoras d^2 = l^2 + w^2 + h^2
Identify and calculate angle between a slant edge and base plane
keyPoints: Project the line onto the plane to locate the right angle on the base
Redraw the vertical cross-sectional triangle as a clean 2D sketch before calculating

lessons.title: Column Vectors, Magnitude & Vector Algebra
objectives: Add, subtract, and multiply vectors by scalars
Calculate vector magnitude |v| = sqrt(x^2 + y^2)
keyPoints: Vector AB = OB - OA (Position vector of B minus position vector of A)
Two vectors are parallel if one is a scalar multiple of the other: v = k * u

lessons.title: Vector Geometry & Collinearity Proofs
objectives: Express geometric paths in terms of given basis vectors a and b
Prove points A, B, and C are collinear by showing AB = k * BC and sharing point B
keyPoints: To prove points A, B, C are collinear: show AB = k * BC and state that B is a common point
Divide ratio segments: if P divides AB in ratio 2:3, then AP = 2/5 AB

lessons.title: Reflections, Rotations & Negative Scale Factor Enlargements
objectives: Enlarge shapes with negative fractional scale factors through a given centre
Fully describe transformations without combining multiple operations
keyPoints: A negative scale factor enlargement inverts the shape through the centre of enlargement
Cambridge marks will award zero marks if more than one transformation type is named

lessons.title: Cumulative Frequency Curves, Median & IQR
objectives: Plot smooth cumulative frequency curves at upper class boundaries
Read median, lower quartile Q1, upper quartile Q3, and interquartile range
keyPoints: Interquartile range IQR = Q3 - Q1
Construct box-and-whisker plots from the 5-figure summary

lessons.title: Probability Tree Diagrams Without Replacement
objectives: Construct probability trees for selections without replacement
Compute conditional probabilities P(A and B) = P(A) * P(B|A)
keyPoints: When an item is not replaced, both the numerator and the denominator decrease by 1
Verify branch probabilities from any single vertex sum to 1
